name: Week 28 Pull — Short Bulk-Phase Baseline
description:
**Warmups are baked into each block's notes as a reminder.**

This is the second gym day in the Push → Pull → Legs sequence. Week 27 showed that back-to-back Push and Pull works; if the calendar allows, put the recovery day after Legs, where you prefer it. Chest-supported row, reverse fly and cable crunch stay out so the day can remain short.

**Pull-ups are plain bodyweight** — 4 sets to form failure, 3s eccentric on every rep, straight bar. Log the numbers without chasing them: the recent decline tracks bulk-phase bodyweight gain.

**The DB row pyramid is 75 → 85 → 95.** Incline curl stays **25 right / 20 left, left first**. High cable curl gets the four-set **190 → 200 → 210 → 220** ladder earned last week.

dayOverview.theme: Repeat the clean Week 27 reads without turning them into tests: bodyweight pull-ups with controlled eccentrics, side-specific incline-curl loads, the 75 → 85 → 95 row ramp, 160 pulldowns, 62.5 face pulls, and the four-set cable-curl ladder.

spotlights.why: After months of postural load from rocking and carrying, the face pull finally costs something on the third set at 62.5, proving its worth as the highest‑value pulling work for the shoulder.

dayOverview.rotationPlan: W29 — DB row and incline curl. W30 — return to lat pulldown and chest‑supported row when it comes back in.
watchpoints: 🛑 keep it shy — the cue is the cap: pull‑ups, DB row, lat pulldown, incline curl. Grip and position lifts where the honest ceiling is the rep the cue breaks, not the rep the muscle quits.
🔥 near‑failure last set OK: face pull, high cable curl. Isolation work where form holds at the limit.

**Left‑arm position note:** the left‑side weakness appears only in the incline curl — chest‑supported, upper arm pinned, bicep at its longest. Other pulling movements (high cable curl, DB row, face pull) are clean on the left, confirming the issue is positional, not a general left‑arm problem.
**Face pull finally costs:** 62.5 held for two sets, but the third set showed fatigue — this is the expected progression as the movement becomes a true strength builder.
**Band-pull-apart remains the pull-day shoulder anchor.** Keep the warmup lean; Push → Pull back-to-back was fine in Week 27.

sets.name: Warmup (Pull-up Bar Station)
sets.notes: Band-pull-apart is the pull-day shoulder anchor. Keep the block lean — everything here happens at or near the bar.

exercises.notes: **The shoulder anchor for pull day.** Light band, slow, squeeze the shoulder blades together without shrugging.
Passive hang. **Also your first read on the right shoulder today** — note whether it is quiet.

sets.name: Behind‑Back DB Shrug — Protective Activation (DO THIS FIRST)
sets.notes: Before anything gets loaded. This is the block that keeps the shoulder quiet through pull day.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 40-50lb pair, behind the back, 2 sets.
- Straight up and down, no rolling
- **Squeeze at the top**, slow release
- Neck long throughout

sets.name: Pull‑Ups — Straight Bar, 4 Sets, 3s Eccentric
sets.notes:
**Bodyweight, 4 sets to form failure, 3s eccentric every rep.** Straight bar, not the swivel handles.

**No spotlight, no chase.** The pull-up decline is expected bulk-phase bodyweight gain — log all four sets as ordinary training data.
- **Set ends when the tempo breaks or the shoulders shrug up**
- Three sets is a fine answer if the shoulder is talking

**Reflection:** does the fatigue feel systemic or localized?

exercises.notes:
Bodyweight, 4 sets, **3s eccentric every rep.** Straight bar.
- Set ends when the tempo breaks or the shoulders shrug up
- Log all four numbers without chasing them
- Three sets is a fine answer if the shoulder is talking

sets.name: DB Rack / Bench Block — Incline Curl → DB Row (3 Rounds)
sets.notes:
**Both lifts live at the DB rack and the adjustable benches — take them as one station and do not walk away between them.**

The chest-supported row and reverse fly are out this week, keeping the pull day short.

**Incline curl: 25 right / 20 left, left first.** Keep the established side-specific loads and match reps.
- **Bench at 45°, arms hanging fully behind the body**
- **Do not swing the shoulder forward** to start the rep
- Slow eccentric, full extension at the bottom

**DB row pyramid: 75 → 85 → 95.** One set at each, each side.
- Expect the left to finish around 8 on the 95; no straps
- Chest supported, spine long, no twisting
- Elbow drives back past the ribs
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 25lb right / 20lb left, left first, 3 sets of 10 each side.
- **Bench at 45°, arms hanging fully behind the body** — the stretch at the bottom is the whole reason for the incline
- **Do not swing the shoulder forward** to start the rep
- Slow eccentric, full extension at the bottom

**LOAD:** pyramid 75 → 85 → 95, one set each side.
- **Expect the left to finish around 8 on the 95** — that is the honest grip‑limited number — no straps, and the grip is the point
- **Chest supported on the bench**, spine long, no twisting to finish the rep
- **Elbow drives back past the ribs**, not out to the side
- Slow eccentric, full stretch at the bottom
- **Let the reps creep rather than the load** — the left ceiling moved on its own last time

sets.name: Lat Pulldown 🛑
sets.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Regular lat pulldown machine: **160**
- Cable pulley: **70/side (140 total)**
Pick whichever is free; **note which equipment + number you used in the log.**

160 ran clean across all three sets last time and read notably easy after the pull‑ups. It holds.

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** regular machine **160** · cable pulley **70/side**. Log which.
- **Pack the shoulders DOWN before the elbows move** — blades into the back pockets first
- Bar to the collarbones, chest up
- **Slow eccentric** — that is where 160 got difficult before
- Ribs down, no leaning back to finish

sets.name: Face Pull — Hold 62.5 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:** 62.5, 3 sets of 20.

**Face pull finally costs:** the third set showed fatigue, confirming the movement is now a true strength builder.
- **Pull to the face, not the chest.** Hands finish beside the ears, elbows high and wide
- **External rotation at the end** — knuckles rotate back, like a double bicep pose. That rotation is the part most people skip and it is the part that matters
- **Squeeze and hold for a beat** at the end position rather than snapping back
- **Traps stay quiet.** If the shoulders ride up toward the ears, drop the pin

**Reflection:** does the end‑range external rotation still feel available on the right side, or does it run out earlier than the left?

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** 62.5.
- **Hands finish beside the ears**, elbows high
- **Rotate the knuckles back** at the end of every rep
- Hold a beat, slow return
- Traps quiet

sets.name: High Cable Curl — Ascending to 220 🔥
sets.notes:
**LOAD:**
- Cable column (your 'double column'): **190 → 200 → 210 → 220** ascending, one set each
- Single pulley: **62.5**
Pick whichever is free; **note which equipment + number you used in the log.**

The whole ladder moves up 10 — your call after running 180 / 190 / 200 twice and finding it a good pyramid with room. **Single arm.** The top set is the near‑failure one, which makes the ascending shape self‑limiting.

- **Single arm**, cable high, elbow fixed in space
- **Do not let the elbow drift forward** — the upper arm stays put
- Squeeze at the top, slow return to full extension
- Top set can run near failure

exercises.notes:
**LOAD:** cable column **190 / 200 / 210 / 220** ascending · single pulley **62.5**. Log which.
- **Single arm**, cable high, elbow fixed in space
- **Do not let the elbow drift forward** — the upper arm stays put
- Squeeze at the top, slow return to full extension
- Top set can run near failure

sets.name: Cool‑Down — 5 Min Fascia/Recovery Block (Permanent Every‑Gym‑Day Closing Block)
sets.notes: Five minutes, every gym day. Slow breathing throughout.

exercises.notes: 30s each arm, elbow at MID height. Directly undoes the forward‑shoulder posture.
Passive. Let the shoulders decompress after the pulling.

tips: Log all four pull-up sets as ordinary training data; do not chase the number.
Nothing goes near failure except the face pull and the top curl. This day can be short or regular depending on energy.
The cool‑down stays even when the session gets cut short.
